solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lord too soon meeting premature end

indicators.note: the word is cut off before its natural finish, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: arriving too soon is being early

explanation.surface: A nobleman is struck down before his time.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of that rank is addressed as Lord, so the title stands for the nobleman.

clue.text: Stress English politician possesses — one collapses finally

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
possesses means has
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A stressed English MP is someone who eventually breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a syllable or idea gives it weight and prominence, the same as the noun here.

clue.text: Go round as headless comic

indicators.note: without a head, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: droll means amusing or comic

explanation.surface: Turning around like a comedian who has lost his head.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn over and over or revolve, as a ball does, is to go round.

clue.text: Greek character, very loud, having shown the way, is to be toned down

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
FF is fortissimo in music notation
to have shown the way is to have led

explanation.surface: A noisy Greek who has been leading must now be quietened.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that is muffled has been deadened or softened, made quieter.

clue.text: Some like June and Maureen having short time in health organisation

parts.note: Mo is a pet name for Maureen

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another

parts.note: the NHS is Britain's National Health Service
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Some women, like June and Maureen, get a quick spell in a health service.
explanation.walkthrough: June looks like another woman's name beside Maureen, but it is the definition's example. The NHS is Britain's state health service.
explanation.definitionFit: June is one of the twelve divisions of the calendar year, so a few such are periods of that kind.

clue.text: Under new management, a farm is for e.g. producing dairy product

indicators.note: a business under new management is reorganised, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the abbreviation for for example, its letters used without the stops

explanation.surface: A farm taken over by new owners begins making a dairy item.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a soft fresh French cheese, sold as a creamy yogurt-like product.

clue.text: One toils, getting badly treated — it's most stupid

indicators.note: treated badly means knocked about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A worker slaves away and is mistreated, which is utterly foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Loony means crazy or silly, so its superlative is the most foolish.

clue.text: Times with hold-ups putting the Spanish off

indicators.note: putting something off removes it, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: hold-ups are delays
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Periods of delay put Spanish travellers off.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods or eras, as in 'in my day', are times.

clue.text: Somehow got influence, bending the knee

indicators.note: done in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gained sway by kneeling before the powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the act of kneeling briefly in worship or respect, as before an altar.

clue.text: A lonely OAP got involved in branch of earth science

indicators.note: letters that are involved are tangled up together, so the words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A solitary pensioner has taken up a field of geology as a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got involved' reads as the pensioner's action, but 'got' belongs to the anagram fodder and 'involved' alone signals the mixing. OAP is old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of fossils sits within the geological sciences, dealing with ancient life preserved in rock.

clue.text: I hate that element of roughness!

indicators.note: an element is a part, so only a portion of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in disgust at a coarse texture.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of disgust or loathing, the noise someone makes at something they detest.

clue.text: Pack bits and bobs?

definitions.meaning: to pack is to cram or fill something tightly
miscellaneous odds and ends, assorted things

explanation.surface: Is it time to box up all the odds and ends?
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cram something full; as a noun it means assorted things or belongings.

clue.text: A Parisian leading a hundred crazy males in America

indicators.note: these letters go in front of the rest

parts.note: un is French for a, the word a Parisian would use
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Frenchman heads a hundred wild men in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in stars and stripes is the personification of the United States government.

clue.text: Section of good chaps getting put outside

indicators.note: one word is placed around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to put something down is to set it
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A part of the group of decent fellows is being shown the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a part or division cut off from a whole, like a piece of an orange.

clue.text: One in mad cult troubles about certain religious writings

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A member of a crazed sect causes trouble over some scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Talmud, the body of Jewish law and commentary, which is a set of sacred writings.

clue.text: Come to the throne maybe and do well

definitions.meaning: to follow a monarch as ruler, with 'maybe' marking it as one example of taking over a position
to prosper or achieve one's aim

explanation.surface: An heir becomes monarch and thrives in the role.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is following another into an office, such as the crown; the other is achieving success.

clue.text: A word of warning — daughter has very negative emotion

parts.note: anger is a strong, hostile feeling

explanation.surface: A warning: a daughter is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs reading this word caution people of a hazard ahead.

clue.text: Big US gangster bringing death

parts.note: big in girth is fat
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A hefty American mobster proves deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one gangster but splits into an adjective and a first name: Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal causes death, like a mortal wound or a deadly accident.

clue.text: First-class introduction to rousing song

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: An excellent opening leads into a stirring anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune or melody, as in Bach's Air on the G String, is a song.

clue.text: Appeal to Desmond, offering some poetry

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal or invocation, as in 'O Lord'
Des is a short form of Desmond; the run of letters across 'to Desmond' is a coincidence, since 'Appeal' must supply the O

explanation.surface: A plea to a man called Desmond comes with a few verses.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'to Desmond' looks like a hidden word, but 'Appeal' must give its letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject, like Keats's, make up a body of verse.

clue.text: TV doctor with a call for restraint

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the BBC series

explanation.surface: A television medic urges someone to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the shout used to make a horse stop or slow down, or to tell anyone to steady on.

clue.text: Being identified, somehow hide in disgust

indicators.note: done in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged anyhow

explanation.surface: Someone who has been recognised covers their face in revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told apart from others is to have been recognised or singled out, as when one thing is discerned from another.

clue.text: Academic class remains unruly

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A university tutorial is still out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A small university teaching group meeting for discussion with a tutor is this kind of session.

clue.text: Refuse to walk endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter is taken off

parts.note: to march is to walk in step

explanation.surface: Someone declines to keep on walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun (REF-use): waste.
explanation.definitionFit: The residue of skins and pips left after pressing grapes, the waste distilled into brandy, has this name.
